# X509 certificate implementation slice

The public class uses unchanged Node v26.13.0 `internal/crypto/x509.js`.
Its native owner is an actual ncrypto `X509Pointer` parsed with the declared
OpenSSL library. Input view byte ranges are borrowed only during synchronous
parse, or copied atomically for shared input; the parsed certificate retains
no JavaScript input, context, or borrowed view. Native class identity and
reserved slots establish the brand. Foreground finalization releases the
C++ wrapper and shared material, whose ncrypto owner frees the certificate.
Internal constructor copies share parsed material and keep independent Node
wrapper caches. Dates, buffers, inspection, descriptors, public validation,
subclassing and lazy caches come from the pinned wrapper and real native
results.

This slice covers PEM/DER construction, subject/issuer/escaped SAN and AIA,
validity strings and dates, CA, fingerprints, key usages, serial and signature
identifiers, raw DER, PEM/JSON, inspection, public-key extraction, issuer
metadata checks, private-key matching and certificate-signature verification.
`checkIssued` does not establish a trust chain; `verify` verifies the supplied
public key against the certificate signature and does not establish trust.
Key extraction/checks reuse the existing actual native KeyObject owner.

Host/email/IP matching, issuer-chain attachment and traversal, legacy
certificate conversion and structured clone/worker transport remain
implementation gaps. Those gaps are not platform boundaries. The adapter
reports unsupported native operations; it does not manufacture metadata or
claim these paths pass. Cross-realm native wrapping, genuine SpiderMonkey GC,
OpenSSL OOM paths, mutable shared input races and all four guest hosts require
validation with an identified engine artifact.

The native allocation ledger tracks the actual requested `sizeof` material
allocation shared among owners, plus SpiderMonkey's associated wrapper size.
The shared-pointer control block and OpenSSL's internal allocations are not
measured by this slice. DER length,
logical result size and RSS are not substituted for those allocations. A
complete OpenSSL allocator/accounting design remains independent work.

`x509-sources.json` records whole unchanged upstream files and source identity.
The ncrypto files are references to the exact library contract, not a second
library implementation compiled by the core bundle. Source preparation or a
native component linked to Node's OpenSSL does not establish guest ABI,
SpiderMonkey compilation, Wasm link correctness or runtime conformance.
